chunks: ‘Ali ibn Ḥusain ibn Mūsā narrated to me from ‘Ali ibn Ibrāhīm ibn Hāshim, from his father, from Ibn Faďďāl, from Abī Jamīlah, from Muḥammad ibn ‘Alī Al-Ḥalabī, from Abū ‘Abdillāh (peace be upon him)

regarding His saying, ‘Then neither did the heavens weep over them, nor the earth, nor were they granted respite.’ He (peace be upon him) said, ‘The heavens did not weep over anyone since Yaḥyā ibn Zakariyyā was killed, until Ḥusain (peace be upon him) was killed, so they wept over him.’
ai.seo_question: Why did the heavens weep for Imam Husain but not for others?
ai.summary: Imam al-Ṣādiq (peace be upon him) interprets the cosmic silence described in Surah Ad-Dukhan (44:29) as a period of mourning suspended between the martyrdom of Yaḥyā ibn Zakariyyā and that of Ḥusain ibn ‘Alī. This hadith from *Kamil al-Ziyarat* highlights the unique ontological status of Ḥusain, asserting that the heavens and earth only resumed their weeping for him, thereby elevating his martyrdom to a universal, cosmic event that reawakened creation's grief. This connection underscores the Shia belief in the continuity of divine mercy and sorrow through the Ahl al-Bayt.
